title: Review: Carbocation stability and Markovnikov; Addition polymers and disposal
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR14#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR14#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR13#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR13#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR13#N.3, OR14#N.3, OR13#N.8a, OR14#N.16, OR13#N.9, OR14#N.13, OR13#N.6, OR14#N.5. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Polymer
items.clue: A very long molecule made of many small molecules joined by covalent bonds.

items.label: Repeating unit
items.clue: Section with two main-chain carbons and extension bonds at each end, e.g. –CH₂–CHCl–.

items.label: Tertiary carbocation
items.clue: The most stable type of C⁺ species, with three alkyl groups bonded to the charged atom.

items.label: Unsymmetrical alkene
items.clue: Its two C=C carbons carry different groups, so HBr can add in two ways, as with propene.

questions.stem: Which carbocation is the most stable?

options.text: CH₃⁺
CH₃CH₂CH₂⁺
CH₃CH⁺CH₃
(CH₃)₃C⁺

questions.explanation: This is tertiary: three alkyl groups on the positive carbon. Tertiary carbocations are the most stable.

questions.stem: Propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, forms the addition polymer poly(propene), written as [repeating unit]ₙ. Which option gives the repeating unit and describes it correctly?

options.text: –CH₂=CH(CH₃)–, keeping each monomer's C=C
–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–, one unit of a single long chain
–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–, all three carbons in the main chain
CH₃CH₂CH₃, one of n separate small molecules

questions.explanation: One bond of each C=C breaks and the two former C=C carbons form the main chain, with CH₃ as a side group. [–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–]ₙ represents one chain containing n of these units.

questions.stem: 2-methylpropene, (CH₃)₂C=CH₂, reacts with water in the presence of an acid catalyst. What is the major organic product?

options.text: 2-methylpropan-1-ol, as H adds to the C with fewer H
2-methylpropane-1,2-diol, as OH adds to each carbon
2-methylpropan-2-ol, via the tertiary carbocation
A 1:1 mixture of the two possible alcohols

questions.explanation: H⁺ adds to the CH₂ end, giving the tertiary carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺, the most stable possible. Water bonds to it and loses H⁺, giving mainly (CH₃)₃COH.

questions.stem: Poly(propene) can be heated until soft, moulded into a new shape, and cooled. The same plastic can be remoulded many times, and its chemical properties do not change. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Heating breaks C–C bonds in the chains, and new C–C bonds form in the new positions on cooling.
Heating turns the chains back into propene molecules, which polymerise again as the plastic cools.
Heating overcomes the forces between chains, which re-form on cooling; no covalent bonds break.
Heating breaks the covalent bonds between neighbouring chains, and these re-form on cooling.

questions.stem: 1-methylcyclohexene is a six-membered ring with one C=C. One C=C carbon carries a CH₃ group and no H; the other carries one H. It reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the major product, and why?

options.text: 1-bromo-1-methylcyclohexane, as H adds to the CH carbon of the C=C, giving a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane, as H adds to the carbon carrying the CH₃ group, giving a tertiary carbocation
1-bromo-2-methylcyclohexane, as Br goes to the carbon with more space around it
Equal amounts of both, as the ring makes both carbons of the C=C equivalent

questions.explanation: With H on the CH carbon, C⁺ is on the ring carbon bearing CH₃: three alkyl groups, tertiary. Br⁻ bonds there, so Br and CH₃ share a carbon.

questions.stem: A council burns mixed plastic waste, including PVC, to generate electricity. Which extra step deals with the main problem caused by burning the PVC?

options.text: Sorting out the PVC first and sending it to landfill instead, as it cannot be burned
Passing the waste gases through a base to remove the hydrogen chloride formed
Burning the plastics with less air, so that less carbon dioxide forms
Cooling the waste gases, so that the chlorine condenses and can be collected

questions.explanation: The chlorine in PVC ends up as HCl, a toxic, acidic gas. A base such as calcium oxide neutralises it before the gases are released.

questions.stem: 2-methylbut-1-ene, CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃, reacts with hydrogen bromide. What is the major product, and why?

options.text: 1-bromo-2-methylbutane, as it forms via a tertiary carbocation
2-bromo-2-methylbutane, as it forms via a tertiary carbocation
2-bromo-2-methylbutane, as Br adds to the carbon that has more H atoms
1-bromo-2-methylbutane, as the primary carbocation is less crowded, so it forms faster

questions.explanation: H adds to the CH₂ end (C1). The C⁺ on C2 has three alkyl groups: tertiary, the most stable. Br⁻ bonds to it: CH₃CBr(CH₃)CH₂CH₃.

questions.stem: A section of an addition polymer is –CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–. Which is the monomer?

options.text: (CH₃)₃CH
CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃
(CH₃)₃COH
(CH₃)₂C=CH₂

questions.explanation: The repeating unit is –CH₂–C(CH₃)₂–. Restoring the C=C between the two main-chain carbons gives (CH₃)₂C=CH₂, 2-methylpropene.
